title: Enhancements: Read build log and logcat with current info
body:
When using Claude with the Jetbrains MCP, I frequently run into build errors. Claude cannot see the errors linted in open files. If I build the project, these syntax errors will go into the build log. I would love to be able to tell Claude "look at and correct the build errors" and have it be able to read the erorrs. At the moment in Android Studio, IT IS NOT POSSIBLE TO COPY PASTE THE DATA FROM THE BUILD LOG WHICH IS CRAZY! The workaround is to take a screenshot of the build errors and paste them to Claude - to his credit he reads them very well but it takes more tokens than would simply reading the text. So please either make it possible for the MCP to see these errors or make it possible to manually copy the errors OR BOTH! :-)  .... Bonus if, via MCP Claude could just see the linting errors

Similar request for LogCat, but a few more details. I CAN copy this text, but would love not to. LogCat contains tons of unnecessary detail that just wastes tokens for an LLM though. I'm talking about the timestamp on every single line like this: "2025-04-06 11:12:48.184 11626-11626". It is not possible as far as I can see to edit what LogCat outputs, again crazy. This timestamp is not useful. I know the calendar date etc. Really all that should be required is minutes:seconds:millis because that is the time range over which a build is relevant. I don't even know what the 11626-11626 is supposed to mean, but it is also not needed. Then there is also the name of the project - I know the name of my project, I don't need it in the information that Claude needs to read. So really all that's needed is shortened timestamp, calling function, log message. If there could be an MCP filter command that would format whatever logs are currently in the window (I will clear the log and just take a small action that contains the interesting error) and then send to Claude to troubleshoot that would be awesome. Now, when I'm running out of context window, I have to copy past and post process LogCat in the way I described using regex in Notepad++ and then paste to Claude. I could maybe write a custom Python action that would do this processing and ask Claude to run an action from the action number, but would prefer if the MCP would just allow me to ask Claude to "look at and correct the LogCat errors" that would be great! Also, please MAKE IT POSSIBLE TO FILTER LOGCAT MESSAGE IN THE DESCRIBED WAY. I  know it's possible to filter logcat but not in this useful way. Thanks for a great MCP server and IDE!
author: braddo99

title: Running configurations using Golang does not return error
body: Run_configuration always returns ok immediately, without waiting for build or tests to be run, and there is not way to see the output of the tests. This makes impossible for agent to use IDE configurations to validate it's actions.
author: iliakonnov

comments.body: I stumbled upon that too. `run_configuration` will just start a configuration without waiting for anything. But in reality we all expect a message about outcomes of command execution and not just execution itself.
Yes, currently we do not wait for execution done. Should we wait for console output?
I was trying to make agent use my configuration to run tests and validate this action. In this scenario console output is crucial. Be it compilation error or some failed tests.

@batya239 it seems to me like the main purpose to run or build the application by MCP Server is to not just start the action, but to receive the result of action execution and to be able to investigate the output afterward.

In version 1.0.26 of the plugin, we improved `run_configuration` tool such that it now waits 120 seconds and return the result back to the requestor. Please give it a try. If it doesn't work for you please drop a comment!

title: Add node-fetch import to resolve "fetch is not defined" error
body:
# Add node-fetch import to resolve "fetch is not defined" error
This PR adds a necessary node-fetch import to the MCP proxy server code to resolve the `ReferenceError: fetch is not defined` error that occurs when running the server on some Node.js versions.
## Problem
When running the MCP server on Node.js versions before v18, which don't have native fetch support, the server fails with:
`CopyReferenceError: fetch is not defined`
This happens because the server uses ES Modules and references the fetch API directly without importing it.
## Solution
Added an explicit import for node-fetch at the top of the file:
```javascript
import fetch from 'node-fetch';
```
This ensures compatibility with older Node.js versions while maintaining full functionality with newer ones.
author: matjanos

comments.body: We don't want to support Node 16 since this version is past the end of life.

title: Force IPv4 usage by replacing localhost with 127.0.0.1
body:
## Description
This PR fixes a common issue where the MCP server fails to connect to JetBrains IDEs when using `localhost` which resolves to IPv6 (::1) while the IDE is only listening on IPv4 (127.0.0.1).

## Changes
- Modified `findWorkingIDEEndpoint()` to use `127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost`
- Added explicit IPv4 usage in the endpoint URLs

## Related Issues
- Fixes #4 - "Error: Specified IDE_PORT=63342 but it is not responding correctly"
- Fixes #5 - "No available MCP tools"

## Testing
Tested with:
1. Claude Desktop configured with `github:Farzoo/mcp-jetbrains#feature/force-ipv4`
2. JetBrains IDE (Rider) with MCP Server plugin 1.0.11
3. Both default port (63342) and custom port configurations
4. Successfully fixed the IPv6/IPv4 connection issues

The configuration used for testing:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jetbrains-ipv4": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "github:Farzoo/mcp-jetbrains#feature/force-ipv4"
      ],
      "env": {
        "LOG_ENABLED": "true",
        "IDE_PORT": "63342"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

comments.body: in windows and pycharm i used a different port 63341 which allows me to flag can accept external connections, then set as envviroment variable the same port and it worked!

Can you please explain the solution in more detail? I am struggling at the same point.

EDIT:
1. Go to Settings > Build, ... > Debugger > set port to 63341 > allow external connections & apply changes 
2. Set env with IDE_PORT: 63341 in the config and run restart claude.

PS: Readme has a small error regarding evn var settings: the env block should be part of the jetBrains block.
